reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, post-fix stale re-review batch 0, 2026-08-02

samples_reviewed.question_text: How many items are there in total?
The two parts are 2 and 1. What is the total?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency names two framings, 'counting up' and 'putting together', but the nine samples lean almost entirely on putting-together content, e.g. seed 84's 'The two parts are 2 and 1. What is the total?' and seed 55's item-count visual; the number-line item at seed 50, 'Show 1 + 2 on the number line,' displays a static sum rather than a start-and-count-forward narration.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: No sample uses an explicit 'start at X, count up Y more' narration, the literal counting-up strategy the competency names alongside putting-together; the number line at seed 50 shows the sum '1 + 2' as a static display rather than a start-and-count sequence.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Every stem, from seed 42's four-word 'What is 2 + 1?' to seed 85's short narrative 'Maria says: 1 + 1 = 1. Is Maria correct?', stays within a single simple sentence appropriate for Grade 1 Quarter 1.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Six distinct rendering shapes appear: mcq facts (42, 43), true/false (44), cloze (45, 46), a number-line display (50), a pictorial item-count (55), a parts-whole frame (84), and error-detection (85), giving genuine format variety for illustrating the sum.

competency_alignment.rationale: Every one of the nine samples, from the number-line display at seed 50 to the error-check at seed 85, targets addition directly with no drift into an unrelated skill like subtraction or place value.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every one of the nine samples produces a sum of at most 3 -- e.g. seed 42's '2 + 1', seed 84's parts '2 and 1' totaling 3 -- so despite the competency's stated ceiling of 20, no sample in this packet approaches even a single two-digit sum.
